text:
Anya M. (sec): Heads up: product wants to drop cluster-admin for private-deploy operator in the next patch. We need a hardened plan for (A) offline/verifiable audit exports for air-gapped customers, (B) how the operator will perform required tasks without cluster-admin, and (C) a KMS fallback model for sites that block our control-plane egress. Thoughts?

Ravi K. (infra): Strong +1 to removing cluster-admin. Migration approach: introduce narrowly scoped CRDs and dedicated Role/ClusterRole per function the operator actually needs (e.g., credentials-manager, rollout-controller). We'll create a compatibility layer that maps legacy calls to new roles during a transition window.

Omar V. (platform): For offline audit I propose "sealed audit bundles": daily tarballs of signed records plus an index file with a chain hash. A minimal record looks like: 

```
{"ts":1729901234, "actor":"operator", "action":"apply/rolebinding", "prev":"<hex>", "sig":"base64sig"}
```

Store at `/var/lib/redwood/audit/sealed/YYYY-MM-DD.tar.sig`. Include a compact manifest that lists head hash and signature algorithm. This lets compliance run an offline verifier.

Sofia H. (sec-eng): Implementation notes: the signing key MUST be protected. For on-prem we support three modes: (1) HSM-backed key (recommended), (2) customer-provided key material wrapped by their HSM, (3) ephemeral software key with documented residual risk. We'll detect available TPM/SEV and prefer hardware-backed keys.

Priya L. (compliance): On the attestation side we need a consistent artifact: image digest, OS baseline, and a signed node quote (TPM attestation or SEV report). The audit bundle should reference these artifacts by digest. Compliance needs a machine-readable bundle with a short human summary PDF.

Anya M. (sec): Who picks up building the offline verifier CLI and the RBAC negative tests? We need owners and ETAs to include in the release notes.

Ravi K. (infra): I'll own the RBAC negative test suite. Plan: create `operator-min-priv` scenarios that run in CI: create resources, assert allowed actions, then attempt denied actions (verbs like impersonate, certificate sign, escalate). Fail CI on any unexpected allow. ETA: 10 business days.

rbac-bot: lint-pass but 3 exceptions found in `drop-operator-cluster-admin`: `mesh-prober:clusterrole`, `legacy-metrics:rolebinding`, `image-pruner:clusterrole` - manual review requested.

Omar V. (platform): I'll prototype `audit-sealerd` (daemonset sidecar) that collects kube audit log, churns into entries, links via prev-hash, and signs with the node key. Minimal RPC: `GET /bundles?from=...&to=...` returns a `.tar.sig`. Also produce a detached index `bundle.json` for quick checks.

Sofia H. (sec-eng): Network policy and egress considerations: by default block all egress from control-plane pods. Provide a declarative egress whitelist and a maintenance-window token to allow burst uploads. Example NetworkPolicy snippet: 

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: cp-egress-lockdown
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-control
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 192.168.10.0/24  # local kms proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8444
```

Sofia H. (sec-eng): Also add support for rsync over SSH gateway for scheduled uploads. The agent should verify the remote collector host fingerprint and only allow uploads when a one-time maintenance token is presented.

Priya L. (compliance): For the SOC artifact pack require: (1) signed bundle(s) with head hash and verification log, (2) attestation artifacts per node, (3) RBAC negative-test output, (4) applied NetworkPolicy manifests plus a snapshot proving enforcement (conntrack/iptables/eBPF evidence). We should produce a template reporting CSV for auditors.

Anya M. (sec): Edge case: customer refuses any persistent keys. We cannot ship verifiable long-term chains without keys. Proposed approach: create human-anchored mode - ephemeral key pairs rotated daily and an offline manual anchor process where a customer-signed root statement is produced at install time. Document risks and require customer sign-off.

Omar V. (platform): Also consider key escrow mode: customer provides a wrapped key blob (wrapped by their HSM) at onboarding. Our auditchaind will unwrap into memory only and never persist plaintext. For air-gapped installs we accept the wrapped blob via secure transfer during on-site provisioning.

Ravi K. (infra): RBAC test harness details: run scenarios in a kube-in-kube sandbox: create roles, simulate operator actions, verify only listed verbs used. Script will grep audit logs for unexpected verbs and fail on matches. We'll integrate with `rbac-bot` for daily diffs.

rbac-bot: scheduled rbac-diff `drop-operator-cluster-admin` created - cron 03:30 UTC daily.

Sofia H. (sec-eng): Next steps / owners: Ravi -> RBAC harness + CI gates (ETA 2w). Omar -> audit-sealerd daemonset + verifier CLI (ETA 3w). Priya/Anya -> SOC artifact template and high-risk acceptance wording (ETA 1w). I'll produce NetPolicy templates and maintenance-window design (ETA 1w).

Anya M. (sec): Great. Please link PRs into the ticket `SEC-1120`. If anyone hits blocking legal/customer constraints on keys, flag immediately. We'll require signed acceptance for high residual risk. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
